questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Following the 1967 setbacks, internal factional warfare erupted within the Congress party between Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and the powerful conservative organizational party bosses collectively known as the 'Syndicate' (led by K. Kamaraj, S. Nijalingappa, N. Sanjiva Reddy, and Morarji Desai). The conflict reached a climax during the Presidential election of August 1969 following the death of President Dr. Zakir Husain. The Syndicate nominated Lok Sabha Speaker Neelam Sanjiva Reddy as the official Congress candidate. Indira Gandhi retaliated by encouraging Vice-President V.V. Giri to contest as an independent candidate, dramatically appealing to Congress MPs and MLAs to vote according to their 'conscience'. V.V. Giri triumphed, delivering a crushing humiliation to the Syndicate. In November 1969, the Syndicate expelled Indira Gandhi, formally splitting the party into Congress (Organisation) and Congress (Requisitionists). Indira Gandhi converted this organizational battle into an ideological crusade for the poor: she nationalised 14 major commercial banks, abolished the hereditary Privy Purses paid to former princely rulers (26th Amendment 1971), and coined the electrifying slogan 'Garibi Hatao' which swept the 1971 general elections."

Question: What was the iconic, populist campaign slogan championed by Indira Gandhi in the 1971 general elections that countered the opposition's 'Indira Hatao'?

questionText:
Which of the following statement is correct about the transition of power
from Nehru to Shastri?
 
(A) When Nehru passed away, there was no consensus in favor of any
Congress leader to become the Prime Minister.
(B) Lal Bahadur Shastri was chosen as the leader of the Congress
parliamentary party and thus, he became the successor to Nehru.
(C) Nehru never depended on Lal Bahadur Shastri in his last year.
(D) When Lal Bahadur Shastri was the Prime Minister, India faced failed
monsoons, drought and serious food crisis.
 
Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed both statements were correct.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid NCERT facts erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is false while Statement II is factually sound.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Detailed Solution:
When Nehru died in May 1964, Congress President K. Kamaraj forged a unanimous consensus in the party. Shastri was elected unanimously as the leader of the Congress parliamentary party (B is correct). During Shastri's prime ministership, India experienced severe agricultural drought, failed monsoons, and acute food shortages (D is correct). Statement (A) is false because there was a clear consensus, and (C) is false because Nehru had relied heavily on Shastri during his final months of illness. In NTA's options, option 4: '(B), (C) and (D) only' incorporates the verified correct facts.
Hence, option (C) is correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.
